summary: Iteration 11: full XLSX export verification (backend + frontend) for Products, Prices, Library, Orders. Backend pytest 5/5 PASSED: /api/library/export returns application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet with cost_library.xlsx, sheet 'Cost Library' and the exact 10 expected columns; /api/skus/prices/export?date_from=2026-01-01&date_to=2026-12-31 returns .xlsx with sheet 'SKU Prices' and headers starting SKU, Product, then marketplace-avg cols; /api/orders/export?date_from=2026-06-01&date_to=2026-06-30 returns .xlsx with sheet 'Orders' and exactly 19 columns starting order_date_iso, marketplace, channel_raw, order_id, sku. Regression confirmed: /api/templates/asin-mapping and /api/templates/cost still text/csv. Frontend Playwright: logged in as admin, visited /products /prices /library /orders — all four buttons ([data-testid='products-export'], [data-testid='prices-export-button'], [data-testid='library-export'], [data-testid='export-csv-button']) render label 'Export Excel' and trigger a download with the correct filename pattern: product_performance_2026-08-18.xlsx, sku_prices_2026-08-18.xlsx, cost_library_2026-08-18.xlsx, orders_2026-08-18.xlsx. Files opened successfully with openpyxl showing correct sheet names (Product Performance / SKU Prices / Cost Library / Orders) and column counts (13/38/10/19).
critical_code_review_comments: The [data-testid='export-csv-button'] selector on Orders page is kept for backwards-compatibility per spec, but the label now says 'Export Excel' and it downloads .xlsx — the testid name is misleading. Consider renaming to 'orders-export' in a future cleanup so testids match user-visible behaviour.

Client-side Products export builds the xlsx in the browser via dynamic import('xlsx'@0.18.5) while the other three go through the backend. Bundle-size impact is deferred until the button is clicked (dynamic import), which is good; just be aware Products XLSX generation happens client-side and thus is limited by browser memory for very large datasets.
Orders endpoint uses openpyxl write_only Workbook (streaming) — correct choice for the 6.6k+ row dataset; confirmed 669KB file produced in <2s.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (4/4 downloads verified as valid xlsx workbooks)

context_for_next_testing_agent: All four XLSX export endpoints & buttons are green. Backend endpoints: GET /api/library/export, GET /api/skus/prices/export, GET /api/orders/export return XLSX. CSV templates (/api/templates/asin-mapping, /api/templates/cost) intentionally remain CSV. Playwright download events work; verify saved files with openpyxl.load_workbook in bash (openpyxl not installed inside the automation runtime).
